text:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: New incident (ID INC-49876) 1: sudden p99 spikes and intermittent streaming stalls observed for /v1/stream on redwood-3-int8 (us-west-2). Auto-paging oncall.

liam_oncall: ack, I'm on. Seeing p95 jump from ~300ms to ~900ms, p99 hitting 3.8-5.2s. Multiple streaming sessions report chunk pauses ~2-6s. Triage starting.

maya_ops: capturing quick metrics: worker gpu-21 showing high dequant_lock_wait median 120ms, occasional peaks 700ms. KV cache miss rate up 4x on keys with long session contexts. Network seems stable.

sophia_ml: note: yesterday we promoted an INT8 calibration (profile: cal-2026-03-29) across us-west-2 to improve throughput. Early telemetry matched perf but didn't exercise sustained long-context streaming at scale. Hypothesis: calibration altered tensor reorder/kernels unlocking path, increasing critical-section contention under many long-lived streams.

devon_infra: mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback of int8 profile to cal-2026-03-15, 2) traffic split to redwood-3-fp16 for streaming route, 3) bump KV service autoscale and reduce max concurrency per GPU, 4) enable dequant lock backoff parameters. We can sequence 1 then 2.

liam_oncall: executing (1) rollback now. If we don't see improvement in 3 minutes, switch streaming traffic to fp16 fallback. Also open a temporary rate-limit for sessions > 4096 tokens.

maya_ops: running rollback cmd:
```
redwoodctl model profile rollback --model redwood-3-int8 --profile cal-2026-03-15 --region us-west-2 --force
```

tom_support: customer impact: 9 orgs reported degraded streaming, 2 customers on escalation (beta chat product). Notifying them with "investigating" template.

sophia_ml: I've kicked the control-plane rollback; serving jobs are rolling. Also enabling an experiment to log dequant_lock_owner and queue depth for postmortem.

maya_ops: rollback acknowledged at 4987655400. Telemetry: p95 trending down to ~360ms; p99 falling toward ~820ms. Streaming stalls frequency dropping. Still seeing isolated gaps on contexts >8192 tokens.

devon_infra: routing rule prepared to divert streaming route when tail_p99>1500ms to redwood-3-fp16. I can apply if rollback doesn't fully clear in 5m. Also increased kv service replicas by +1 to reduce hot locks.

liam_oncall: hold off on routing for now, monitor for 10m. Add temporary alert: dequant_lock_wait > 250ms for >2min.

rachel_ce: please add the two escalated customers to the incident timeline and share ETA. I'll prepare CE comms for 11:30 PT.

tom_support: updating tickets: "Mitigation in progress: rollback applied. Monitoring. Temporary token-rate limit may be applied for very long sessions."

sophia_ml: logs we captured for the problematic period: 
```
[2026-03-30T22:58:12Z] worker=gpu-21 ERROR dequant_lock wait=512ms ctx_tokens=6144 conns=72
[2026-03-30T22:58:14Z] kvsvc WARN miss key=session:ctx:zzz123 hit_ratio=0.64
[2026-03-30T22:58:16Z] stream WARN gap_detected session=sess-42 gap_ms=3800 chunks=3
```

maya_ops: observed that stalls correlate to sessions with >4k tokens and high concurrent streamer count. Suggest adding long-context canary tests to the calibration pipeline.

devon_infra: also found a minor bug in dequant lock metrics where queue depth underestimated by ~20% when multiple locks nested. We'll patch metric exporter after incident.

liam_oncall: status: mitigated -> monitoring. p95: ~330ms, p99: ~720ms, stall counts back near baseline. Action items: 1) require long-context workload in calibration rollout (automation), 2) add dequant_lock_wait alerting, 3) verify metric exporter fix, 4) create fallback traffic-split runbook.

rachel_ce: noted. Please include impacted accounts list and expected follow-up timeline in postmortem. CE will reach out to customers once postmortem link available.

tom_support: marking tickets as "monitoring" and requesting logs for all affected sessions.

incident_bot: INC-49876 updated: Mitigated; paging cleared.

liam_oncall: I'll draft the incident postmortem and runbook updates. Drop any extra telemetry or customer notes here. Thank you everyone.
